Bone safety for dogs depends on the type of bone, how it is prepared, its size, and supervision. Large raw beef or bison bones are generally considered safer than cooked bones, which can splinter and cause injury or blockages [d1,d2,d4,d7]. Raw chicken bones can also be safe if large enough to prevent choking, but cooked bones of any kind should never be given [d6]. Commercial synthetic chews are a safer alternative when in doubt [d1]. Regardless of the bone type, always supervise your dog and choose appropriately sized pieces to reduce risks like dental fractures or intestinal damage [d3,d5,d7].
